title: Language and cognitive development
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how language works in the mind and brain and how thinking develops from infancy: the parts of language, speech perception and production, word recognition and sentence processing, the brain networks for language and aphasia, language acquisition and its theories, bilingualism, reading and dyslexia, infant perception and cognition, Piaget, Vygotsky and modern views, theory of mind, and the debates about nature and nurture.
primary_reading: The Noba Project psychology modules (free online)

weeks.1: The parts of language: sounds, words, sentences and meaning
weeks.4: Language in the brain and aphasia
weeks.6: Theories of acquisition: nativist, statistical and usage-based
weeks.10: Piaget, Vygotsky and modern views of development
weeks.11: Theory of mind and social cognition

blocks.deliverable: Analyze a sentence at each level of language.
Compute transitional probabilities in a supplied syllable stream.
Week 7 midterm; evaluate a claim about bilingual advantages.
Design a looking-time experiment and say what it can show.
Write a balanced analysis of one nature–nurture debate.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Development essay and study plan: write a 2,500-word essay on one question in language or cognitive development (for example whether there is a critical period for language), presenting the strongest evidence and arguments on each side, followed by the design of one study that could move the debate forward.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
